display.purpose: Page titles in the header toolbar. One per view.

headline.purpose: Metric card values and primary data figures where a number leads the eye.

title.purpose: Card headings, modal titles, table column headers.

body.purpose: All prose, list content, form copy, and supporting text at 12px density.

label.purpose: Timestamps, client IDs, status codes, breadcrumb paths. Always JetBrains Mono, never Inter.

shadows.name: flush
shadows.purpose: Default resting state for all cards and panels. Border carries presence.

shadows.name: lifted
shadows.purpose: Interactive cards on hover, focused panels. Barely visible — signals affordance.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Notification dropdowns, command overlays, floating panels above the page.

shadows.name: modal
shadows.purpose: Full dialog modals. Maximum elevation in the system.

motion.name: ease-state
motion.purpose: Default easing for all state transitions (hover, focus, active). 150ms.

motion.name: ease-overlay
motion.purpose: Overlay and modal entrance. 200ms in, 150ms out.

narrative.overview:
The STC Operations Portal is a precision instrument for behavioral health administration. It exists in the same visual register as air traffic control software and medical device dashboards — surfaces where staff make decisions in real time, where information must be found instantly, and where an unclear interface has real operational consequences.

The system uses a tight restrained palette: an indigo accent fires against a cool slate neutral body. White surfaces carry content. Slate gradations handle hierarchy. Indigo activates exactly where action or selection lives and nowhere else. The semantic vocabulary — emerald for success, amber for warning, red for critical — exists to surface alerts instantly, not to decorate.

This system explicitly rejects the consumer SaaS warmth of Notion or Linear, the gamified optimism of health apps, the overweighted analytics chrome of Tableau, and the hostile density of legacy EHR systems like Epic.
keyCharacteristics: Dense but scannable: compact spacing, precise type hierarchy, maximum information per pixel
Neutral baseline with surgical accent use — indigo fires only where selection or primary action lives
Semantic color vocabulary for status: recognizable by convention, never decorative
Flat-to-layered elevation: borders carry resting hierarchy; subtle shadows emerge on state and overlay
Three-register typography: Space Grotesk for scanning, Inter for reading, JetBrains Mono for structured data

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Action Indigo (#4f46e5) occupies ≤15% of any given screen surface. It marks selection and primary action — nothing else. A screen where indigo is used broadly is a screen where nothing important stands out.

rules.name: The Semantic Lock Rule
rules.body: Emerald, amber, and red are status colors, not palette colors. They do not appear on decorative elements, non-status tinted backgrounds, or UI chrome. Seeing red must mean something is wrong.

rules.name: The Three-Register Rule
rules.body: Inter for reading, Space Grotesk for scanning, JetBrains Mono for structured data. Never mix these registers for the same content type.

rules.name: The Density Rule
rules.body: Body text runs at 12px (0.75rem). This is a clinical operations tool where staff read dense information under time pressure. Compact type is not a compromise; it is a feature of the register.

rules.name: The Flat-First Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Shadow appears only on interactive state (hover) or when the surface is genuinely above the page plane (overlay, modal). A card with a shadow at rest uses decoration as depth.

dos: Do use Action Indigo (#4f46e5) exclusively for active state, primary action, and selection.
Do pair every status color with labeled text: emerald = present/complete, amber = expiring/warning, red = critical/overdue.
Do use JetBrains Mono for timestamps, client IDs, status codes, and breadcrumb paths.
Do keep all primary content surfaces white (#ffffff). Let slate-50 be the body field.
Do render active navigation as a full indigo-50 background fill — never a left-side border stripe.
Do implement all interactive states before shipping: hover, focus, active, disabled, error.
Do keep body and label text at 12px or smaller.
donts: Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent on nav items, list rows, cards, or callouts.
Don't design to a generic SaaS aesthetic (Notion, Linear, Airtable). This is a clinical operations tool.
Don't import consumer health app warmth (MyFitnessPal, Headspace visual register).
Don't use overdesigned analytics chrome (Tableau-style dense chart panels).
Don't replicate legacy EHR density or visual hostility (Epic, PointClickCare).
Don't use indigo for decorative fills or hover states on non-primary elements.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with a gradient fill).
Don't build identical card grids as the default layout answer.
Don't place small-caps tracked eyebrow labels above every section heading.
